To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a gene called "glial cells missing" encodes a nuclear protein that is expressed transiently in glial cells in Drosophila and that its mutation causes glial cells to become neurons and its ectopic expression causes neurons to become glial.
gcm is a binary switch between neuronal versus glial fate.
a single gene, GCM, is required for the determination of glial cells in the Drosophil CNS and PNS and that it is a binary switch between neuronal versus glial determination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that control the determination of glial cells in the Drosophia CNS and PNS.
the molecular basis for the determination and development of neurons and glial cells in the Drosophia CNS and PNS.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms that control cell fate specification in the Drosophil CNS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gcm is an important factor in glial cell differentiation and function in the Drosophia nervous system.
gcm functions as the first known binary switch that determines neuronal or glial fate in Drosophila.
GCM is a transcription factor that is required for glial cell fate specification in the Drosophia CNS and PNS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gcm is a key regulator that controls the balance between the two cell types in Drosophila.
the Drosophia CNS is a good model to study the molecular mechanism of cell fate determination.
GCM is the first gene identified that is required and sufficient for the specification of glial cells in the Drosophil CNS and PNS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binary switch is a general mechanism for cell fate determination.
glial cells are not just a passive support for neurons but rather have an active role in the development of the nervous system.
the decision of neuronal versus glial fate is made very early in development, and that the decision is made in the same way in the PNS and CNS.
